blocks.text: Ezra 4 does not simply move year by year. It begins with resistance during Cyrus’s reign, surveys later accusations under Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes, and then returns in verse 24 to the stoppage of temple work until Darius. The groups whose offer to help build is refused should also not automatically be identified with the later Samaritan community: the narrative describes local peoples resettled under Assyrian rule, while Samaritan identity and its labels developed over time.

The correspondence continuing in the surrounding passages is written in Aramaic, a language used widely in imperial and regional settings. Its letters and decrees fit that administrative setting, but the language by itself does not show that every document has survived unchanged from a royal archive.
